column4: Visit note | 2025-06-15 04:30 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Priya Paul, 27, female. Ms. Paul presents today complaining of bothersome weight gain and stubborn acne that have troubled her for quite some months. She explains that she first noticed the weight gain after starting a desk job in Banani, which altered her daily routine and physical activity levels. By background, her occupation is listed as a fisherman, though her recent transition to sedentary desk work has contributed significantly to her current concerns. She also reports a past medical history of Bronchial asthma, which is currently stable without recent exacerbations. She denies any severe chest pain, sudden shortness of breath, blurred vision, or abnormal bleeding patterns. Upon physical examination today, her vital signs and anthropometric measurements are recorded as follows: BMI 32.8, BP 113/72 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, and weight 45 kg. Cardiac examination reveals normal heart sounds without murmurs, and her chest is clear to auscultation bilaterally. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment, including a pelvic ultrasound and hormone profile; no new medicine was prescribed at this visit. She was advised to aim for 5 percent weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up is scheduled after the test results are ready.
